open-market-competition-imports.text: The party's plan, presented in July 2026, answers high prices with more competition: dominant suppliers could not control several product lines at once, tariffs would be cut gradually and imports opened. In February 2022 the government Prime Minister Naftali Bennett led presented a package that included cuts to import duties on goods such as flour, olive oil, eggs, meat and fish.

cut-taxes-and-government-spending.text: The party's July 2026 plan centres on competition and cutting tariffs rather than on VAT or income-tax cuts, which the report on the plan does not mention. The package presented in February 2022 by the government Prime Minister Naftali Bennett led did include import-duty cuts and a tax credit for working parents.

active-state-regulation.text: The party's July 2026 plan gives competition and opening imports as its answer to high prices, where your option relies on the state stepping in. Its steps against large companies, such as barring dominant suppliers from controlling several product lines at once, are part of that competition approach.

direct-support-for-households.text: In February 2022 the government Prime Minister Naftali Bennett led presented a package that mixed direct help for households, such as a tax credit for working parents and after-school subsidies, with import-duty cuts. The party's current plan, from July 2026, centres on competition and imports, and its direct support is for farmers, so this is a secondary element of its position.

emergency-powers-shin-bet.text: The party shares part of your answer: its personal-security plan would define crime as a security threat and bring in the Shin Bet (Israel's internal security service), and its Negev plan adds the Shin Bet to a joint task force. The research found no position on the new power to hold suspects without trial that your answer also includes.

more-police-resources-normal-law.text: The party's plans define crime as a security threat and bring in the Shin Bet, which your option leaves out, and its Negev plan sets minimum sentences by law. The plans do share a national operation to collect illegal weapons and stronger neighbourhood policing.

invest-in-arab-communities-first.text: On 24 October 2021, the cabinet led by Prime Minister Naftali Bennett approved NIS 29.5 billion over five years for developing Arab society alongside NIS 2.4 billion against crime. The party's current plans focus on enforcement, so investment is a secondary element of its position.

resume-fighting-full-control.text: The party's national security plan promises an ultimatum that Hamas disarm or be disarmed, and a rule of attacking whenever Hamas builds up or trains. It does not call for a return to full-scale war now, says it has no interest in running Gaza, and does not mention settling Gaza or encouraging residents to leave.

hold-positions-disarmament-first.text: The party's national security plan says it will not move one millimetre from the yellow line until Hamas is fully disarmed. On 1 August 2026, party leader Naftali Bennett opposed the Board of Peace framework and said Israel must not budge from the red line until Hamas is disarmed.

advance-international-arrangement.text: On 1 August 2026, party leader Naftali Bennett opposed the Board of Peace framework, which sets out how Hamas would disarm and the army withdraw, and said agreements must not be signed over Israel's head. The party's plan instead holds the current line until Hamas is disarmed and removes Qatar and Turkey from any role in Gaza.

end-war-full-withdrawal.text: The party's national security plan holds the army at the current line until Hamas is fully disarmed and sets a rule of attacking whenever Hamas builds up or trains. In August 2026 party leader Naftali Bennett said Israel would preserve freedom of action in Gaza.

defeat-hamas-then-security-control.text: The party's plan shares the ultimatum that Hamas disarm or be disarmed, says it has no interest in running Gaza, and does not mention settling it, while party leader Naftali Bennett said in August 2026 that Israel would preserve freedom of action there. The research places this as a secondary element, since the party does not call for a return to full-scale war now.

anchor-torah-study-exemption.text: The party's Those Who Serve Law plan would require military or full civilian national service and cancel benefits such as the kollel stipend for those who do not serve. This is its 2026 position: in January 2022, as prime minister, Naftali Bennett voted for a bill that kept the exemption for yeshiva students and lowered its age from 24 to 21.

gradual-targets-by-agreement.text: Like your option, the party offers benefits to those who serve, and in September 2026 party leader Naftali Bennett proposed Haredi hesder yeshivas along the borders combining Torah study with service. It differs on the gradual approach: its national security plan says everyone will enlist, without exemptions, and its Those Who Serve Law plan cancels benefits for those who do not serve.

universal-service-with-sanctions.text: The party's Those Who Serve Law plan would require military service or full civilian national service and cancel benefits for those who do not serve, and party leader Naftali Bennett repeated this on 6 October 2026. The research notes that his rejection of any exemption quota makes his position stricter than your option's allowance for a small number of Torah scholars.

voluntary-service-for-all.text: The party's Those Who Serve Law plan would require military or full civilian national service and cancel state benefits for those who do not serve, and on 6 October 2026, party leader Naftali Bennett said they will not receive a single shekel. It does also promise benefits to those who serve.

speed-up-planning-and-construction.text: The party's housing plan includes moving planning powers to local authorities with a target of a building permit within three months, and cutting urban-renewal projects from 10-15 years to five. These are two of the plan's seven measures, and the research says the plan gives none priority.

state-led-affordable-rental.text: The party's housing plan includes building 100,000 long-term rental homes within ten years, 40% of them at 30% below market rent, with tax incentives for long leases. It is one of seven measures, and the research says the plan gives none priority.

direct-help-for-buyers.text: The party's housing plan gives active reservists a benefit worth NIS 1 million toward a first home or a better one, plus priority in land tenders. It is one of seven measures, and the research says the plan gives none priority.

develop-periphery-and-transport.text: The party's housing plan sets a national goal of one million more residents outside the centre of the country within ten years, with investment in transport, jobs, health and education there, and faster urban renewal. The plan has seven measures, and the research says it gives none priority.

military-pressure-until-threats-removed.text: The party's national security plan says that if Hezbollah strikes Israel, Israel strikes Iran, and in June 2026 party leader Naftali Bennett rejected US limits on Israel's freedom to act against Hezbollah. The research calls the evidence mixed, since the plan also seeks normalization agreements, and found no document taking a position on the current ceasefires or on withdrawing from southern Lebanon.

force-plus-us-backed-agreements.text: The party's plan promises to strengthen the Abraham Accords, restore the Negev Summit and bring normalization with Saudi Arabia and other countries, which overlaps with your option. The research calls the evidence mixed: the plan also rests on constant military pressure, and in June 2026 party leader Naftali Bennett rejected US limits on Israel's freedom to act against Hezbollah.

prioritize-ending-multifront-war.text: The research describes the party's approach as constant military pressure and keeping freedom of action: its plan says that if Hezbollah strikes Israel, Israel strikes Iran, and in June 2026 party leader Naftali Bennett rejected US limits on Israel's freedom to act against Hezbollah. The research found no document taking a position on the current ceasefires.

end-military-operations-regional-peace.text: The party's national security plan says that if Hezbollah strikes Israel, Israel strikes Iran, and it pairs this with political, economic and information pressure on Iran's regime. The research found no document taking a position on the current ceasefires or on withdrawing from southern Lebanon.

full-sovereignty.text: In May 2021 Naftali Bennett told his party that as prime minister he would not apply sovereignty to territory, and in an interview published on 3 July 2026, he described settlement under the law in Area C with the Palestinian Authority running Areas A and B. He does support settlement in Judea and Samaria.

partial-sovereignty-area-c.text: In an interview published on 3 July 2026, party leader Naftali Bennett described settlement under the law in Area C, with the Palestinian Authority running Areas A and B, which overlaps with your option. He differs on sovereignty: in May 2021 he said he would not apply it, and the party's national security plan has no section on applying sovereignty.

maintain-current-situation.text: In May 2021 Naftali Bennett told his party that as prime minister he would continue the existing policy of no sovereignty and no new settlements, while not freezing construction in existing communities. In an interview published on 3 July 2026, he described his plan as the same as the existing arrangement and said he is against a Palestinian state.

separation-two-states.text: In an interview published on 3 July 2026, party leader Naftali Bennett said he is against a Palestinian state and called it a red line. In a recording published on 7 September 2025, he said he supports autonomy for the Palestinians but not sovereignty over the borders.

two-states-pre-1967-border.text: In an interview published on 3 July 2026, party leader Naftali Bennett said he is against a Palestinian state and called it a red line. In a recording published on 7 September 2025, he said he opposes giving up land.

one-equal-state.text: The party's documented approach is different: in a recording published on 7 September 2025, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett said he supports autonomy for the Palestinians but not sovereignty, and in July 2026 he described Israeli security control over Areas A and B.

continue-judicial-changes.text: According to a Ynetnews overview from 22 September 2026, the party proposes repealing the 2025 law on choosing judges and defining the powers of the Knesset, government and Supreme Court in a basic law. Your option instead gives elected officials more power over the courts.

broad-agreed-constitutional-framework.text: According to a Ynetnews overview from 22 September 2026, the party proposes a basic law on legislation setting when the Supreme Court may intervene, and the Declaration of Independence as a basic law. party leader Naftali Bennett signed the 26 September 2026, principles document assigning constitutional matters to a joint working group.

repeal-changes-protect-independence.text: According to a Ynetnews overview from 22 September 2026, the party proposes repealing the 2025 law on choosing judges, as your option does. The research treats this as secondary, since the main theme of party leader Naftali Bennett's statements is a constitution or basic law defining each branch's powers.

keep-current-system-stability.text: According to a Ynetnews overview from 22 September 2026, the party proposes repealing the 2025 law on choosing judges, which your option would keep. It also proposes a basic law defining the powers of the Knesset, government and Supreme Court.

state-commission-under-existing-law.text: party leader Naftali Bennett has repeatedly pledged that a government he leads would set up a state commission of inquiry immediately, including at the joint list's launch on 26 April 2026, and at the slate launch on 6 September 2026. The legal term he uses refers to a commission whose members the President of the Supreme Court chooses under existing law.

commission-appointed-by-knesset-balance.text: party leader Naftali Bennett has repeatedly pledged an immediate state commission of inquiry, including at the launch on 26 April 2026, a model whose members the President of the Supreme Court chooses under existing law. The research found no statement in which he discusses alternative ways of choosing the members.

commission-chosen-by-neutral-mechanism.text: party leader Naftali Bennett has repeatedly pledged an immediate state commission of inquiry, including at the launch on 26 April 2026, a model whose members the President of the Supreme Court chooses under existing law. The research found no statement in which he discusses alternative ways of choosing the members.

strengthen-jewish-character.text: The party's plan keeps the Chief Rabbinate but ends its exclusive control, proposes a civil partnership covenant, and lets each local authority decide on public transport on Shabbat. Conversion would stay under Orthodox standards, but with powers returned to community rabbis.

keep-status-quo.text: The party's plan keeps the Chief Rabbinate, as your option does, but ends its exclusive control, proposes a civil partnership covenant and lets each local authority decide on public transport on Shabbat. In October 2021 the government Prime Minister Naftali Bennett led also advanced a kosher-certification reform allowing private bodies to certify.

more-choice-local-decisions.text: The party's plan keeps the Chief Rabbinate but ends its exclusive control, proposes a civil partnership covenant, recognises international kosher certifications and lets each local authority decide on Shabbat transport. It would keep conversion under Orthodox standards, with powers returned to community rabbis.

separate-religion-and-state.text: The party's plan shares a civil partnership covenant open regardless of religion and local decisions on public transport on Shabbat. It differs by keeping the Chief Rabbinate, though without its exclusive control, and by keeping conversion under Orthodox standards.

points.text: Party leader Naftali Bennett has said the first topic his cabinet would discuss is a basic law limiting a prime minister to two terms or eight years, and on 22 November 2021, as prime minister, he voted for a government bill limiting a prime minister to eight years at its first reading, though it did not become law.

Party leader Naftali Bennett proposes merging the state, state-religious, Haredi and Arab school streams into one system with a shared core of 60% of study time, with schools that do not teach the core losing state funding.

The party's LGBT equality plan includes a ban on conversion therapy, immediate and equal registration of both parents, and a Basic Law: Equality protecting against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, and party leader Naftali Bennett said in September 2026 that the time has come to pass these laws.
